pairs.subject: translation-pipeline-topology
pairs.evidence: scripts/i18n/guide-drift.mjs:102 The guide pipeline keeps its own hardcoded locale list instead of deriving it from the repo's language registry (LANGUAGES in src/i18n/localeRelease.ts). Adding or removing a language therefore means editing a second file, so the guide pipeline and the switcher can drift apart; the per-locale guide translations are also committed to master as LLM output with no recorded review.

techniques.evidence: scripts/i18n/guide-drift.mjs:102 This is the 'convenience copy' the technique names. LANGUAGES in src/i18n/localeRelease.ts:31 is the registry, but the guide drift checker, the status emitter (emit-guide-status.mjs:114) and getLocalized.test.ts (`GUIDE_LOCALES as readonly Language[]`) all read this separate list.

src/data/guide/locales/ar/_meta.json:5 An LLM subagent translated the bodies (translate-guide-subagent-prompt.md), and they are committed to master next to the canonical English. The _meta.json records a model but no reviewer, and I found no review-wave gate. That makes the commit an unbacked review claim, which is the trust-class laundering the technique names.

src/data/guide/getLocalized.ts:166 It falls back per whole unit and never splices. A stale or unverified topic serves the whole current English unit, with the older translation one tap away (TranslationNotice). English short-circuits at line 139 without loading any locale module or the status table, so the canonical path is unchanged.

src/data/guide/locales/ar/_meta.json:8 Each topic is pinned to a digest of the exact English unit it was translated from. guide-drift.mjs anchors each pin against git history, and refresh mode re-translates only the topics whose English changed. Caveat: the engine id lives beside the key at locale level (`translator`), not inside the key.

scripts/i18n/translate-guide-subagent-prompt.md:38 The request is a declared contract: Action (full/refresh), Surface, Units (key plus title/description/body), whole-category neighbours, and glossary terms applied per occurring unit. Refresh mode is fed by the drift work order.

scripts/i18n/translate-guide-subagent-prompt.md:3 The whole guide corpus goes through one subagent flow. There is no enumerated set of hand-authored exception pages and no separate exception registry to judge.

scripts/i18n/translate-guide-subagent-prompt.md:169 The units are whole Markdown documents, not catalog values, so there is no value-level classification to do before a request is built. Identifiers inside the prose are protected by an instruction to the engine instead.

pairs.registryProposal: The guide here is a whole-corpus committed translation that uses the hand-authored-exception-contract's staleness mechanism: a per-unit pin of the canonical revision, anchored against history, with a generated status table that demotes stale units to canonical. The standard names that mechanism only for the exception pages. It could say that it also discharges the update obligation for a reviewed-and-committed corpus.
